builds.scope: Runtime library, Electron main/shared/preload and renderer compiled locally. Desktop archive contains compiled inputs with external Electron/Node/native dependencies, not an installable native app. The fixture-mode e2e journeys (managed-provider no-fallback, managed-agent-run) ran on this build on macOS against the contract-fixture endpoint with the labeled e2e fixture native port; that is no GUI or native qualification. The endpoint-mode e2e cases were type-checked only.

archiveValidation.scope: SHA-256/SHA-512, sidecars, manifests, member sets, safe paths and every payload hash verified before extraction. Every relative import of the platform endpoint client (main/enterprise/endpoint-client), the e2e fixture port gate (main/enterprise/e2e-endpoint-native) and the dispatch harness with the Cue shell route rule (main/enterprise/dispatch) was redirected to the compiled desktop archive, and every import of the provider route evidence consumer (managed/provider-route), the endpoint native port rules (managed/endpoint-port) and the library index to the public runtime bundle; five suites (provider-route-evidence, endpoint-native, e2e-endpoint-native, dispatch, provider-conformance) ran on those bytes. Turn, Codex request, Cue shell executor, host, service and conformance suites stay source-only. Public declaration checks and a plain Node load of both archives (a non-receipt refused, approval fails closed with no verifier, per-platform transports and address rules, macOS with no native port refused, the fixture port installed only unpackaged under NODE_ENV=test with the explicit variable, an SSH shell route needs the enrolled endpoint of its remote) passed. Temporary identity-only pin leaves the historical runtime pin unchanged.

tests.boundary: Local typed-port and public-schema fixtures, the labeled contract-fixture endpoint daemon, temporary data directories and recording sinks only. No signed production route receipt, trusted verifier, real provider, native peer or live endpoint supplied authority.

behavior: A signedProviderRouteQualification v1 is consumed against the exact launch candidate (provider, adapter, transport, binary, OS, backend, input digest), every published allow and deny case and bounded freshness; approval needs a host-injected verifier and fails closed (no verifier, refused or lost verification, cancellation, a candidate change across the await, a node-harness tier), with no fallback and no lease minted.

A managed real-provider launch (runAgentTurn with a route ceiling) requires a qualified route for the turn provider on the transport the final spec runs on (ssh, pty or cli-process), the approved credential set and a sandbox backend; a mismatch is managed-denied before the verifier, an unavailable approval managed-unavailable, both before admission and spawn.
Persistent Codex SDK requests naming a foreign thread or turn are declined without asking; per-request effects stay under ManagedEffectAuthority.

A Cue shell route takes the same evidence for the cue-shell provider on its own transport; an SSH action must carry the enrolled endpoint of the very remote the wrap resolved. No runner passes one and no production verifier exists, so both shell routes stay unsupported under management.

The endpoint is opened through the platform client on desktop and detached host: a Unix socket on Linux and macOS, a local named pipe only on Windows; on macOS and Windows a NATIVE-ENDPOINT/1 port must name the serving process (pid, birth digest, executable digest, principal) for each connection before a byte is written. No production port is installed, so macOS and Windows managed endpoints stay unavailable; a labeled fixture port exists only for unpackaged NODE_ENV=test builds with MAESTRO_E2E_ENDPOINT_NATIVE=fixture.

contractMappings.remaining: Route-qualification key distribution, the canonical inputDigest encoding, the dispatch snapshot field for route evidence and the per-platform endpoint address and server identity are unpublished; the consumers are implemented behind local seams and not advertised. Production provider and native actions still require authenticated negotiated authority.
